floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 24 -> 23, three scheduling-barrier cheats removed; CSE store-to-load forwarding identified as the single mechanism, volatile axis permanently killed (sandbox strips it).

frontier.hypothesis: Some condition in cse_insn makes GCC 2.7.2 decline to RECORD a QImode MEM destination in the value table while still CSE-ing its address, and that condition is what lets the target share one lui/addiu base between a block's reload and its store without the store being forwarded into the reload.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c dest-recording block in cse_insn - candidate triggers are a subreg SET_SRC, a mode mismatch between the recorded value and the QImode mem, a zero_extract (bitfield-insert) SET_DEST, or do_not_record being set by the address. A bitfield container is the strongest candidate: 0xF8 plus three single-bit flags is exactly a ':1,:1,:1,:5' shape.
frontier.next_probe: grep -n 'in_memory|invalidate|GET_CODE (dest) == MEM' tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c and read cse_insn's dest-recording block to identify the exact condition; then declare 0x80106A73 as a 3x1-bit + 5-bit bitfield struct and measure. Mind that this fork allocates bitfields HIGH-first (.claude/rules/bitfield-direction-divergence.md), so the field order is constrained by which mask bit is which.

frontier.hypothesis: The objdump-level inferences above can be confirmed or replaced outright by reading the RTL, and doing so is cheaper than further spelling sweeps.
frontier.mechanism: cc1 -da emits .cse / .combine / .greg dumps; the .cse dump shows directly whether the sb's MEM is entered into the value table and the .combine dump shows whether the %lo fold is combine's doing or the expander's.
frontier.next_probe: Run cc1 with the build flags plus -da on the sandbox's preprocessed input for code6cac_b, write the dumps to tmp/grind/func_80034F88/s2/, and read the .cse and .combine dumps around the three sb insns of func_80034F88.

frontier.hypothesis: 0x80106A70..0x80106A73 was one declared object in the original source (a 4-byte array or a struct), and re-deriving it as such changes every address expression in the function at once.
frontier.mechanism: A single declared object gives one base for the whole region, which is the only untried change that touches both the flag blocks and the copy loop simultaneously; it also changes which addresses combine can fold.
frontier.next_probe: Introduce a single declaration covering the region (keeping the existing extern names as the split-out view for the other users at src/code6cac_b.c:4032 and :4044 so the diff stays scoped), spell the flag byte and the copy destination through it, and measure. Abort early if the emitted addressing shows 3(base) displacements, since target has none.
